# UKIP 2015 Manifesto Summary

## Core Vision and Philosophy

The UKIP 2015 manifesto presents itself as offering a transformative moment in British politics—the first real opportunity for change in a century. The party positions itself as fundamentally different from establishment parties, claiming to represent ordinary British citizens who feel successive governments have stopped representing their will. Central to this vision is the belief that Britain is "big enough to make our own laws" and sovereign enough to control its own borders, tying this directly to the 800th anniversary of Magna Carta.

## EU Withdrawal: The Central Pillar

Brexit forms the foundation of virtually all UKIP policies. The party commits to an immediate in/out referendum, followed by activating Article 50 for an orderly two-year exit. They argue EU membership costs Britain £9 billion annually in direct contributions while strangling British business with excessive regulations and undermining British sovereignty. The manifesto dismisses the "three million jobs" myth about EU membership, characterizing such claims as deliberate deception by the pro-EU lobby.

## Immigration Reform

UKIP presents immigration as fundamentally about "space, not race," arguing the current system is broken and discriminatory—favouring EU citizens over Commonwealth countries. Their solution is an Australian-style points-based system treating all nationalities equally. Key proposals include a five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration, limiting skilled worker visas to 50,000 annually, and requiring five years of tax contributions before migrants can access benefits or the NHS.

## Economic Policies

The party pledges fiscal responsibility while promising significant tax cuts: raising personal allowance to £13,000 (removing minimum wage earners from income tax), abolishing inheritance tax, raising the 40% threshold to £55,000, and increasing transferable marriage allowances. They would fund these through leaving the EU, cutting overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, and replacing the "unfair" Barnett Formula.

## NHS and Social Care

UKIP commits £12 billion additional investment over five years, funding 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 nurses, and 3,000 midwives. They would end "health tourism" by restricting NHS access to those with five years of UK tax contributions, abolish hospital parking charges, and repeal the EU Working Time Directive which they claim harms medical training.

## British Values and Culture

The manifesto explicitly rejects multiculturalism as causing "alarming fragmentation of British society," instead promoting integration and the English language as binding forces. UKIP pledges to make St George's Day a bank holiday, uphold freedom of speech against the "culture of offence," and combat practices like forced marriage and FGM through mandatory reporting requirements.
